question.prompt: Let \(f\) be a function for which \(f\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) = x^2 + x + 1.\) Find the sum of all values of \(z\) for which \(f(3z) = 7.\)

solutions.explanation:
To use the given rule for \(f(3z)\), the input \(x/3\) must equal \(3z\). Set \(x=9z\), giving
\[
f(3z)=(9z)^2+9z+1.
\]
Therefore \(f(3z)=7\) exactly when
\[
(9z)^2+9z-6=0.
\]
Treating \(9z\) as a single quantity makes the factorization straightforward:
\[
(9z+3)(9z-2)=0.
\]
A product is zero exactly when at least one factor is zero, so the only solutions are \(z=-1/3\) and \(z=2/9\). Both give valid real inputs. Their sum is
\[
-\frac13+\frac29=\boxed{-\frac19},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Match the function input and factor
